text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we didn't fully vet power-cut during the artifact/symlink swap. thought: two-slot layout + activation journal. want to capture failure/resume states.

marta: Yep. RFC covered two-slot mostly, but recovery during rename/boot is fuzzy. need a concrete state machine.

sam: Kernel-level race: if the swap happens while initrd is mounting, we can end up half-configured. We should rely on something the bootloader/initrd reads, not just a runtime symlink.

tim: Proposed flow: 1) write new image into inactive slot 2) write signed slot manifest and fsync 3) write pending-activate marker to small activation partition and fsync 4) perform atomic rename of /srv/active -> /srv/active.bak and put new link in place 5) on first-boot initrd reads activation partition, verifies signature, clears marker on success. prevents silent partial switch.

julia: For air-gapped installs, firmware tweaks (efibootmgr) are risky. prefer activation partition on same media (ESP or small metadata partition) so initrd can trust it without remote.

ops-bot: note: duplication costs — large model artifacts mean we can't naively copy full image twice on limited disks. consider reflink/cow or streaming chunk-apply.

alex: Agreed. plan: chunked content-addressed store so we only transfer new chunks. staging uses overlayfs to assemble slot. activation is then just a cheap rename. also need merkle per-image for partial-validate/resume.

marta: Important: signature verification must be resumable. write verification progress to activation partition so if powercut happens during verify we continue rather than restart full verify.

sam: Edge-case: powercut after atomic rename but before marker cleared. On next boot, initrd will see pending-activate and should complete verification; if verification fails, initrd should roll back symlink to previous slot and mark the new slot broken.

tim: rename(2) is atomic only within same filesystem. ensure /srv/slots and /srv/active live on same mount. layout rule: all slots under /srv/slots on single FS. use mv -T or rename syscall.

julia: Example ops snippet (will add to RFC):

```
# stage into inactive slot (chunked/rsync style)
rsync -a --inplace --no-compress chunks/ /srv/slots/slotB/
sync && echo fsync-stage > /dev/null
# write signed manifest to activation partition (double-buffered)
write_manifest /dev/mapper/activation "{\"slot\":\"slotB\",\"seq\":42,\"sig\":\"...\"}"
# atomic switch using rename within same FS
ln -sfn /srv/slots/slotB /srv/active_tmp
mv -T /srv/active_tmp /srv/active
```

sam: initrd hooks: on early init read activation partition, verify manifest sig, verify merkle of slot chunks (resume if partial), if OK drop marker and continue boot; else roll back to previous slot and mark failure.

marta: Manifest format decision: small JSON with fields {active_slot, seq, sig, prev_seq}. Write double-buffered at fixed offsets so a single powercut won't leave half-manifest. Incremental seq enables detection of torn writes.

ops-bot: suggestion: use two copies + CRC + seq. if both copies invalid, fallback to factory slot (slotA). :thumbsup:

alex: Rollback policy: if validation fails twice, mark slot as quarantined and send operator alert. For on-prem we'll expose admin CLI to force-recover. For hosted we'll surface telemetry.

tim: Disk-full during staging: refuse install if free_space < threshold (model_size * 0.25 + slack) OR enable streaming apply that evicts old cache chunks as new ones written. Implement quota check in the packager.

julia: Also consider a tiny write-ahead log on activation partition that lists operations (copy-chunk X done). That lets resume without full re-verify if we trust per-chunk checksums.

sam: Security: verification keys are in initrd's trusted store (rotate via KMS/HSM at pre-provision time). For airgap, key rotation is operator-managed — note this in ops runbook.

marta: Action items: alex -> update RFC with manifest layout + double-buffer plan; sam -> initrd verification state machine + resume logic; julia -> example scripts + chunked packager changes; tim -> FS layout and rename guarantees doc; I'll own rollout/test matrix.

alex: I'll add explicit failure scenarios to RFC (powercut during manifest write, during rename, after rename before first boot, during verify) and propose deterministic recovery for each. scheduling a follow-up sync next Tue 10am. thanks! :rocket:
